pageOrderNote: This PDF's internal page order does NOT match the paper's own printed footer numbers ('Page N of 16'). PDF pages 9 and 12 are swapped relative to the printed sequence — PDF page 9 carries printed footer 'Page 12 of 16' (Section B start), and PDF page 12 carries printed footer 'Page 9 of 16' (Q26-30). Every other PDF page matches its printed number exactly (checked all 16). Confirmed by reading footer text on every page, not assumed. The correct READING ORDER by printed page is: PDF 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,12,10,11,9,13,14,15,16. Stage C MUST use this order (or the printed footer numbers, which are reliable here) to reconstruct question sequence — using raw PDF page order would put Section B's physics short-answer block in the middle of the Section A MCQs.
notes: Genuine scanned board paper (bilingual, SI Code 212 letterhead, Set Code D) — not a case like F5 (2018-b). No printed answer key anywhere in the 16 pages (confirmed after reading all pages), same as pilot paper 2016-a and 2018-a — Stage E will need textbook/RAG route for all objective questions.

Handwritten dot marks (•) appear next to one option per MCQ throughout Section A, same phenomenon as F3 (2016-a pen-ticks) — per the established F3 rule these are never treated as an answer source, only recorded as a flag on the affected questions.

Q12, Q13, Q14 (page 6) and Q17, Q18 (page 7): the Hindi question stem/options are genuinely too blurred to transcribe in the source scan — tried re-rendering at 400/500 DPI with cropping, confirmed it is a source-scan defect, not a rendering resolution problem. English text on the same questions is clear and was used; Hindi is marked illegible rather than guessed, per Stage B rule ('nahi dikh raha to confidence low + note, guess mat karo').

Q20 (page 8) repeats Q19's question stem verbatim ('The spinal cord originates from') instead of a new question — a genuine duplication printed in the source paper itself, transcribed as-is. Flagging for Stage C/D to decide how to handle (likely: not usable as a distinct question, or needs the real Q20 sourced from another year's repeat if this is a known repeat question).
Page 2's right margin has a few stray character fragments bleeding in from an adjacent page/column in the scan — excluded from transcription as a scan artifact, not this paper's content.

Page 13, Q6: the printed Hindi asks for 'Lenz ke dahine haath ka niyam' (Lenz's right-hand rule) while the printed English on the same line says "State Fleming's left-hand rule" — a genuine Hindi/English mismatch in the source paper (different rule AND different hand), transcribed exactly as printed on each side, not reconciled.
